answer: Each agent may book only one wind-tunnel lane, tied to a single falcon: a pitot-static probe whose factory serial cannot be restaked. To be paid, the agent files a quill: an unused hash of a twenty-second turbulence trace plus the probe's one-time authenticator. Traces that line up, or a serial under two keys, collapse to one payout and the later bond is slashed. The probe must sit in a registered velvet grommet during the run; the grommet's compression print is folded into the hash, so a replayed trace fails, and one probe cannot occupy two grommets at once.
